# Briefly

> Briefly is AI software for wealth advisors, a web app a firm signs into from a browser. We set it up for the firm and connect Salesforce and Outlook. It keeps a current picture of each client with every line linked to its source, writes briefs before meetings and follow-ups after, flags idle cash and drift once the custodian or portfolio management system is linked, and reviews a prospect's statements before the first call. $150 per seat per month.

Briefly is a web app your firm signs into. Your client data stays in a private environment for your firm on AWS. The AI models that read it run on zero-retention terms and never train on it. Nothing goes into Salesforce until an advisor approves it. Briefly makes suggestions for the advisor to review, and the advisor makes every decision and every recommendation. Briefly also comes as a connector for Claude Desktop, for teams that already work there.

The web app also runs agents on a schedule and emails each finished report with a PDF attached. It includes a market brief agent, a firm view built from the firm's CIO notes, and the firm's logo and two colors on every agent output.

Briefly is built by Briefly Wealth LLC, founded by Connor Florczyk.

These files are intended to help LLMs and AI agents accurately ground answers about Briefly in primary source pages rather than third-party summaries. For a flat plain-text concatenation of the main marketing pages, see `/llms-full.txt`.

## Product

- [Home](https://www.brieflywealth.com/): Briefly is AI software for wealth advisors. A web app set up for your firm, with a current picture of each client, briefs before meetings, follow-ups after, and prospect analyses, every line linked to its source. $150 per seat per month.
- [Knowledge base](https://www.brieflywealth.com/knowledge-base): How Briefly builds a knowledge base from a firm's own documents, email, meeting notes, and portfolio data, with every fact traceable to its source.
- [Compare](https://www.brieflywealth.com/compare): The Briefly web app and the Claude connector side by side, including scheduled runs with emailed reports, firm view, the market brief agent, and your brand on every agent output. Both read from the same client record, cited and correctable.

- [ChatGPT and Claude compliance for financial advisors](https://www.brieflywealth.com/ai-compliance-for-financial-advisors): What Reg S-P, the SEC, and FINRA require before an advisor puts client data into ChatGPT or Claude, and what advisors use instead.

## Examples

- [Sample deliverables](https://www.brieflywealth.com/sample-deliverables): Six real Briefly deliverables, a prospect analysis, a quarterly review, a goal analysis, a month-end letter, a deal summary, and a correction-loop example, with names and firms fictionalized.
- [Sample prospect analysis](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-prospect-analysis): Nine checks run against a prospect's two statements, split into findings the documents prove and questions to ask, with the skipped checks and unverified items named.
- [Sample quarterly review](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-quarterly-review): Performance for the quarter, allocation drift against policy, and the conversations worth having next, cited back to the source documents.
- [Sample goal analysis](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-goal-analysis): Each goal priced against a household's actual accounts, with funding gaps named and every figure traceable to a statement.
- [Sample month-end commentary](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-month-end-commentary): A month-end letter showing household totals, what moved since last month, and the market backdrop, written for the client and cited for the advisor.
- [Sample deal summary](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-deal-summary): Terms, traction, and the three biggest risks of a private deal, condensed into a one-page brief a committee can act on.
- [Sample correction loop](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-correction-loop): How one detail from a meeting note becomes a standing rule Briefly applies to every brief after. Names and firms are fictionalized.
- [Sample Morning Brief](https://www.brieflywealth.com/sample-brief): A sample edition of Briefly's Morning Brief email, with a pre-market table, an advisor talking point, and what to watch that week. Illustrative, not real client data.

## Blog

- [Blog](https://www.brieflywealth.com/blog): Writing on advisor workflows, portfolio prep, and client communication from the Briefly team.
- [The Jobs AI Won't Replace](https://www.brieflywealth.com/blog/jobs-ai-wont-replace): Advisors, lawyers, and doctors stay hard to replace because the value in the work is trust, judgment, and accountability, not information processing. Published December 17, 2025.
- [Your Brain Doesn't Have Enough RAM](https://www.brieflywealth.com/blog/your-brain-doesnt-have-enough-ram): Advisors hit a real memory limit managing 100-plus households, and the fix is surfacing the right context at the right time instead of trying to remember everything. Published January 3, 2026.
- [The Great Wealth Transfer Trap](https://www.brieflywealth.com/blog/great-wealth-transfer-trap): As wealth splits across heirs, an advisor's assets under management can stay flat while the number of relationships to manage multiplies, straining the economics of the book. Published November 5, 2025.

## Newsletter

- [Morning Brief subscribe](https://www.brieflywealth.com/subscribe): A daily weekday email covering what moved overnight, what's on the calendar, and a talking point advisors can use with clients that day. Free for financial advisors.
